entries.clue: Polish admirer, nude (4)

blocks.note: to polish a surface by rubbing, a verb
an enthusiast, as in a film fan
naked, from the idiom 'in the ___' for wearing nothing

annotation.surface: A description of someone from Poland: a fan who happens to be naked.
annotation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: 'nude' is a third meaning, from the phrase 'in the buff'. The capital P tempts you towards Poland, but it is the verb polish.
annotation.definitionFit: Buff means to polish, an admirer (a jazz buff), and bare skin (in the buff).

entries.clue: Scuba – radar deployed – voracious fish! (10)

indicatorNotes.deployed: deployed means spread out and rearranged into position, so the letters move

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A diver switches on underwater radar and spots a hungry predator.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes keep the surface as a breathless diving story, and the fodder sits right at the start, before the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Barracudas are large, predatory fish known for their aggressive feeding.

entries.clue: Taking LSD, greasy hippies – in the end, they’re in a cell (5,5)

indicatorNotes.in the end: tells you to take only the end, the last letter, of 'hippies'

blocks.note: fatty = greasy
acid is slang for the drug LSD
last letter of hippieS

annotation.surface: Greasy-haired hippies on LSD end up locked in a prison cell.
annotation.walkthrough: The cell is a living cell of the body, not a prison cell; fatty acids are building blocks of its membranes.
annotation.definitionFit: Fatty acids are organic molecules found in every living cell, forming the fats in its membrane.

entries.clue: Straitened, distressed, but back in office (10)

indicatorNotes.distressed: distressed means knocked about, so the letters of 'Straitened' are disturbed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An official who was hard up and upset has nonetheless got their old job back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Straitened' and 'distressed' look like a pair of synonyms for hard times, which hides that one is the letters and the other rearranges them.
annotation.definitionFit: To be reinstated is to be restored to a former post, so back in office.

entries.clue: Nobleman over there at crack of dawn? (5,2)

blocks.note: an earl is a British nobleman
yon is an old word for 'over there', as in 'yonder'

annotation.surface: Someone points to an aristocrat standing some way off at daybreak.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: early on means near the start of anything, and the crack of dawn is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Early on means at an early stage, and the crack of dawn is the early stage of a day.

entries.clue: Buried in Parthenon, a gong, one with straight edges? (7)

indicatorNotes.Buried in: the answer lies buried inside the letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of Parthenon, the word a, and the start of gong

annotation.surface: Someone describes a gong buried in the ruins of the Parthenon in Athens.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark is there because 'one with straight edges' covers any polygon; a nonagon is just one example, with nine sides.
annotation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a nine-sided polygon, a figure bounded by straight edges.

entries.clue: At, sadly, a place of trade stocking American flipping fishy dish (12)

indicatorNotes.stocking: a shop stocking something holds it inside, so MART holds A
indicatorNotes.flipping: flipping turns the whole string over, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
alas = sadly, an exclamation of regret
taken as written
a mart is a market
A is a standard abbreviation for American, placed inside MART to make MARAT

annotation.surface: A sad scene: at some market, a flipping American dish of fish is on sale.
annotation.walkthrough: Build the whole string first, then turn it round. 'Flipping' looks like an expletive, but it is the reversal. Taramasalata is a Greek dip made from fish roe.
annotation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a dip made from salted fish roe, so a fishy dish.

entries.clue: In the auditorium, drew amphibian (4)

indicatorNotes.In the auditorium: an auditorium is where you listen, so it is the word as heard, not as written

blocks.note: drew = towed, as in pulled a cart

annotation.surface: Someone in a theatre sketches a frog-like creature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drew' looks like sketching, but it means pulled along: towed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the toad is a warty, land-dwelling member of the amphibians.

entries.clue: Do be quiet – lolly? (4)

blocks.note: taken as written
sh! = be quiet

annotation.surface: Someone is told to hush while sucking on a lollipop.
annotation.walkthrough: Lolly here is British slang for money, not a lollipop; dosh is another slang word for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Dosh and lolly are both British slang for money.

entries.clue: Curses and rants, being heartless (4)

indicatorNotes.being heartless: heartless means losing the heart, the middle letter

blocks.note: RANTS without its middle letter N

annotation.surface: A cruel person swears and rages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Curses' is the exclamation, like 'damn!', not the verb; rats! is a mild oath.
annotation.definitionFit: Rats! and curses! are both mild exclamations of annoyance.

entries.clue: Way to wear swimwear in major thoroughfares (5,5)

indicatorNotes.to wear: the road puts on the swimwear, so the swimwear goes around it

blocks.note: swimming trunks
a road is a way, as in a street name

annotation.surface: A fashion tip on how to wear your swimsuit on the high street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Way to wear swimwear' reads as fashion advice, but 'way' is a thing that wears, and so sits inside, the swimwear.
annotation.definitionFit: Trunk roads are the main roads of a national network, so major thoroughfares.

entries.clue: ‘Ho! Abruptly draw back, draw back!’ – one who entered tomb (6,6)

indicatorNotes.Abruptly: abruptly means cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.back: the second 'back' turns the pieces before it around

blocks.note: taken as written
draw back = RETRACT, cut short to RETRAC
taken as written

annotation.surface: A cry of alarm as someone recoils before stepping into a tomb.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'draw back' looks like shocked repetition, but the first is a synonym cut short and the second is the word itself plus a turnaround of everything after Ho. Howard Carter opened Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922.
annotation.definitionFit: Howard Carter was the archaeologist who first entered Tutankhamun's tomb.

entries.clue: So began my day, unpredictably: it’s a toss-up (8,4)

indicatorNotes.unpredictably: the letters come out in no predictable order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone recalls a morning that could have gone either way.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: 'it's anybody's game' and 'it's a toss-up' both say the result is uncertain.
annotation.definitionFit: When something is anybody's game, the outcome is as open as a coin toss.

entries.clue: Plans suggested by erotic etchings (10)

blocks.note: technical drawings, or plans generally
blue = smutty, and prints such as etchings

annotation.surface: Someone got their ideas from looking at racy pictures.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage 'blue' means sexually explicit (a blue film), so blue prints are dirty pictures.
annotation.definitionFit: Blueprints are detailed technical drawings, and by extension any plans.

entries.clue: To make greater numbers, is Swedish band touring a capital city? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.touring: a band touring a place travels round it, so ABBA goes around A

blocks.note: adding makes numbers greater
taken as written
ABBA, the Swedish pop group
taken as written, placed inside ABBA

annotation.surface: A question about whether a Swedish group is touring a capital to boost its audiences.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a band pulling bigger crowds, but 'to make greater numbers' is just the arithmetic verb, and the band goes around the lone letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Ethiopia's seat of government is one of the world's capital cities.

entries.clue: Portion of cinnabun, chai: nourishing – and free! (7)

indicatorNotes.Portion of: the answer is a portion of the letters that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of cinnabun, all of chai, and the first letter of nourishing

annotation.surface: A café promises a cinnamon bun and spiced tea that are filling and cost nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like 'no charge' in the café picture, but here it is the verb: to release.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: taking the chains off a captive sets them free.

entries.clue: Swiss multinational and Dutch cosied up (7)

blocks.note: Nestlé, the Swiss food company
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

annotation.surface: A Swiss firm and a Dutch one have become cosy business partners.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as corporate collusion; the answer is a plain word for snuggling.
annotation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly against someone, so nestled means cosied up.

entries.clue: Reckoned was plausible (5,2)

blocks.note: totalled, as a sum
a story that adds up makes sense

annotation.surface: Someone judged that an explanation sounded believable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reckoned' reads as 'thought', but here it means calculated.
annotation.definitionFit: To add up is both to total figures and, of a story, to make sense.

entries.clue: Deal – or collapse (4,3)

blocks.note: to hand out, as a dealer does with cards
to faint

annotation.surface: An ultimatum: accept the deal or fall apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a noun, an agreement, but it is the verb for handing out cards.
annotation.definitionFit: Pass out means both to distribute and to lose consciousness.

entries.clue: Initially Schubert and Liszt’s illustrious educator – renowned Italian! (7)

annotation.definition: Initially Schubert and Liszt’s illustrious educator – renowned Italian!

indicatorNotes.Initially: take the initial, first, letter of each following word

blocks.clueFragment: Schubert and Liszt’s illustrious educator – renowned Italian
blocks.note: the first letter of each of these seven words

annotation.surface: A tribute to the famous Italian who taught Schubert and Liszt.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: Antonio Salieri really did teach both Schubert and Liszt.
annotation.definitionFit: Salieri was an Italian composer who taught Schubert, Liszt and Beethoven in Vienna.

entries.clue: Was hacking, chesty daughter given treatment? (7)

indicatorNotes.given treatment: treated letters are worked on and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
D is the abbreviation for daughter
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A worried parent asks whether their coughing daughter was seen by a doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'hacking' a cough and 'chesty' a symptom; in fact hacking means cutting, and chesty is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To scythe is to cut with a long curved blade, so scythed means was hacking.

entries.clue: Everyman’s describing idiot husband – misguided satire – crazy scenes (4,8)

indicatorNotes.describing: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so MY goes around ASS H
indicatorNotes.misguided: misguided letters are sent the wrong way, so SATIRE is rearranged

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, speaking of himself: my
an ass is a fool
H is the abbreviation for husband
anagram of SATIRE

annotation.surface: The setter describes a foolish husband and a botched satire causing chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's own name stands for MY, the setter's possessive. Put ASS H inside M…Y, then add the rearranged SATIRE.
annotation.definitionFit: Mass hysteria is collective panic or frenzy, producing crazy scenes.

entries.clue: Pasta sauce in uniform covered with bit of old cloth (4)

indicatorNotes.covered with: in a down answer, a covered piece sits below what covers it, so RAG goes on top of U

blocks.note: a rag is a scrap of old cloth
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A uniform stained with pasta sauce is covered with an old rag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing, which fits the cloth, but it is the radio code word for U.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragù is an Italian meat sauce served with pasta.

entries.clue: While using phone, removed central part of cable (4)

indicatorNotes.While using phone: on the phone you only hear words, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: to core an apple is to remove its central part

annotation.surface: Someone on the phone cut out the middle of the wire.
annotation.walkthrough: The phone is the homophone signal, not part of the picture: 'removed central part of' is one word, cored, which sounds like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A cord is a flexible electrical cable, like a phone cord.

entries.clue: Character seen towards end of The French Lieutenant’s Woman? (10)

annotation.definition: Character seen towards end of The French Lieutenant’s Woman?

blocks.note: the surface wants a person in the novel; the setter means a typographic character, a punctuation mark

blocks.clueFragment: towards end of The French Lieutenant’s Woman
blocks.note: read the title as printed type: near its end, between Lieutenant and s, sits a mark

annotation.surface: A question about a figure who turns up late in John Fowles's novel The French Lieutenant's Woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as a person in the novel, but it is a typographic character: the apostrophe in Lieutenant’s, near the end of the title.
annotation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation character, and one appears near the end of the book's title.

entries.clue: Irish musician in African country, needing no introduction (4)

indicatorNotes.needing no introduction: the introduction is the first letter, which is dropped

blocks.note: KENYA without its first letter K

annotation.surface: A famous Irish singer, so well known she needs no introduction, is in Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' is a stock phrase for a celebrity, but here it lops the first letter off KENYA.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Donegal-born singer and composer is famous for layered new-age music.

entries.clue: Actor, waiting where Cluedo weapon concealed? (10)

blocks.note: an actor waiting to stand in for the lead
the Study is one of the rooms in Cluedo

annotation.surface: An actor hangs around backstage wondering where the murder weapon was hidden.
annotation.walkthrough: Cluedo is the British name of the board game Clue, where you name the killer, weapon and room; one room is the Study. The question mark flags the whimsical second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: An understudy is an actor who waits to replace the lead performer if needed.

entries.clue: Eats pilaf regularly – here? (4)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

blocks.note: every second letter: eAtS pIlAf

annotation.surface: A guess about where people eat rice pilaf as a staple.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: pilaf is a rice dish eaten widely across Asia, and the question mark admits it is not the only place.
annotation.definitionFit: Pilaf is a staple rice dish across much of Asia.
